Pixel sprite format (v1)

A sprite is one JSON file: a character grid, a legend that maps characters to xterm-256 colours, and optional palette tiers. It is data only, so any client can read it with a stock JSON parser. sprite.schema.json is the contract; examples/slime.json is a full example.

This repository is the home of the format. The schema's $id is its published URL: https://lowlysre.github.io/gh-pixel-editor/spec/sprite.schema.json

Fields

FieldRequiredMeaning
versionyesAlways 1. Clients reject other values.
nameyesLowercase kebab-case id.
mirrornotrue: rows is the left half and the right half is its mirror.
rowsyesOne character per pixel, no whitespace. . is transparent. A short row pads with its last character (before mirroring).
legendyesCharacter to colour. An integer is a flat colour. An array is a ramp, dark to bright, that the renderer lights.
lightingnodither (default 0.9) and rim (default 1.6).
tiersnoTier number to a partial legend. Entries listed replace the base legend; others are kept.

Colours are xterm-256 indices (0-255). Truecolor is not representable.

Grid rules

  1. Apply mirror: pad each row to the widest row, append its reverse.
  2. If the row count is odd, append one transparent row.
  3. A character missing from the legend uses the B entry. A sprite without B must define every character it uses.

Lighting

A ramp pixel at (x, y) in a grid of width w and height h gets a level in 0..n-1 (n is the ramp length):

t     = 0.5 * (1 - x / w) + 0.5 * (1 - y / h)
level = t * (n - 1) + (bayer[y % 2][x % 2] - 0.5) * dither
level -= rim            if any 4-neighbour is transparent or off-grid (once)
level = clamp(round(level), 0, n - 1)
bayer = [[0.0, 0.5], [0.75, 0.25]]

Light comes from the top left, outer edges get a dark rim, and the 2x2 dither turns the gradient into shading. A flat colour is drawn as-is (no lighting) at the brightest shade level (5). Rounding is half to even (Python round).

Reserved characters

CharKindWhy it matters
EeyesFlat colour. Wins a shared cell in solid mode.
TteethWins over void and body in solid mode.
Mmouth/voidDark region; loses to E and T in solid mode.

Every other character is a plain region. . is always transparent.

Rendering targets

TargetRule
halfTwo pixels per text cell: ▀ with foreground (top) and background (bottom).
solidTwo pixels per cell, one colour each. Emit ▀ with foreground = background. When a cell holds two pixels, the winner is chosen by kind: E, T, M, plain. GitHub's log viewer smears two-colour cells, so use this there.
squareOne text row per pixel row; each pixel is one or more block glyphs with foreground = background.
plainNo colour. Shade glyph by level (░░▒▒▓█), @ for eyes, v for teeth, space for void.
svgOne <rect> per pixel (merge horizontal runs), shape-rendering="crispEdges", colour from the xterm-256 table.

Never draw a pixel as a bare space: log viewers drop the background of whitespace-only text.

Authoring for GitHub logs

  • Draw eyes, teeth and mouths at least two pixels tall on even rows so they survive solid pairing.
  • Keep a sprite's height even.
  • Draw text as a label, not as pixels.

Conformance

A client conforms when it validates against the schema and, for the example sprites, reproduces the reference output of the Python renderer (sprites.py in quest-ops) for each target byte for byte. Unknown top-level fields are errors; unknown version is an error.
